function: DDPG jointly learns NOMA channel allocation, device transmit power, and STAR-RIS amplitude and coupled-phase coefficients to maximize the uplink sum secrecy rate (pp. 3, 5).
system: STAR-RIS (energy splitting, coupled phase), 10-20 elements in Figs. 7-8; 1xM channel vectors imply single-antenna BS and devices; jammer, two Eves; Rician fading; band not stated (pp. 3-4, 10).
method: Reinforcement learning: DDPG actor-critic with action mapping, trained by environment interaction; imperfect-CSI variant averages Z noisy channel samples (SAA) in state and reward (pp. 5-7).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rician fading on all links, path-loss exponent 2.6, random device positions in a 3-D layout (pp. 4, 8-9); no standard channel model or dataset.
test_conditions: Sweeps over elements, power, devices, jammer power, path-loss factor, CSI error; paper does not state training on one condition and testing on another (pp. 10-12).
baselines: AO algorithm (non-learned); basic actor-critic (AC) RL; system-variant schemes C-RIS, IPS-STAR-RIS, OMA, fixed channel allocation, no-Eve, Eve variants (p. 9).
metrics: Sum secrecy rate (bps/Hz), training reward convergence versus episodes; relative secrecy gain over OMA and C-RIS at CSI uncertainty 0.25 (pp. 9-12).
complexity: Order of complexity as sum of layer-width products of actor and critic, Eq. (35); claimed independent of STAR-RIS elements; no runtime or FLOPs (pp. 8, 10).
q1_support: p. 4: "We adopt the Rician fading channel model for all involved channels"; custom simulator with textbook Rician fading and path loss, the paper never mentions 3GPP, DeepMIMO, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100 or measured data.
q2_support: p. 12: "Fig. 13 presents the convergence performance of Algorithm 2 under different learning rates and CSI uncertainties"; p. 11: "Fig. 11 presents the sum secrecy rate versus the number of IoT devices". Missing: no statement that a model trained on one setting is tested on another, Figs. 7-12 are sweeps.
q3_support: p. 10: "our proposed algorithm based on the DDPG can achieve higher sum secrecy rate than the AC algorithm"; p. 10: "our proposed algorithm performs close to the AO algorithm" (AO is the optimization baseline, p. 9). Fig. 7, sum secrecy rate.
q4_support: p. 8: "The complexity of the Algorithms 1 and 2 can be expressed as" Eq. (35), an O() of products of consecutive-layer neuron counts of the actor and critic networks.
q5_support: p. 8: "a 3-D coordinate network setup is considered"; custom simulation, no code or data link or DOI and no public dataset anywhere in the paper.
notes: Included, area 3: the secrecy-rate objective is not an excluded function, and the learned decision includes the STAR-RIS coefficients. Antenna counts are inferred from 1xM channel vectors (p. 4). AC counted as a standard RL algorithm on the same problem.
